## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical security hardening and disruption management capabilities for CKAD-level Kubernetes deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Container SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem for container isolation
- PodSecurityContext: fsGroup for proper file permissions on PVC-mounted volumes
- Kernel capabilities: drop ALL to minimize attack surface
- PodDisruptionBudget: maintain minimum healthy pods during maintenance
- Rollout and rollback procedures for safe deployments

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
  labels:
    app: api-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api-gateway
    spec:
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1001
      containers:
      - name: api-gateway
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - "ALL"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /srv
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/app
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: api-gateway-pvc
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: api-gateway-config
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api-gateway-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-gateway
```

## Verification & Rollback
```bash
# Verify under load
kubectl exec deployment/api-gateway -- curl http://localhost:8080/health
kubectl top pods -l app=api-gateway
kubectl get pods -l app=api-gateway --watch

# Rollback if needed
kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway
kubectl rollout status deployment/api-gateway
```

- NetworkPolicy egress rules must correctly identify targets; misconfiguration blocks all traffic

kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: collector
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 1000
        runAsGroup: 1000
        fsGroup: 1000
      containers:
      - name: collector
        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "256Mi"
            cpu: "100m"
          limits:
            memory: "512Mi"
            cpu: "500m"

            path: /livez
            port: 8080

        - name: data
          mountPath: /var/lib/collector
        - name: config

---

metadata:

spec:

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses CKAD fundamentals, including CronJobs, PVCs, ConfigMaps, InitContainers, Secrets, TLS sidecars, probes, and NetworkPolicies within a realistic risk-based scenario.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and backoff management
- PVC-mounted configuration discovery
- YAML validation with yq for key extraction
- InitContainers for tool installation and sidecar patterns
- Secrets management and TLS certificate rotation
- Namespace-level network policy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: config-scan
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  schedule: "0 0 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: yq-installer
            image: busybox:1.36
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              wget -O /usr/local/bin/yq https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.35.1/yq_linux_amd64
              chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
          containers:
          - name: scanner
            image: curlimages/curl:latest
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              for cm in $(kubectl get configmap -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
                kubectl get configmap $cm -o yaml | yq e '.data | keys' - | grep -v '^---\|config.json' && echo "$cm"
              done | curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d @- http://config-scan-portal:8080/api/v1/scan
            env:
            - name: API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: config-scan-secret
                  key: api-key
            volumeMounts:
            - name: configs
              mountPath: /configs
          - name: tls-sidecar
            image: nginx:alpine
            ports:
            - containerPort: 443
              name: https
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /ready
                port: 443
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /health
                port: 443
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tls-certs
              mountPath: /etc/nginx/certs
              readOnly: true
          volumes:
          - name: configs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: config-scan-pvc
          - name: tmp
            emptyDir: {}
          - name: tls-certs
            secret:
              secretName: config-scan-tls
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: config-scan-pvc
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadOnlyMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: config-scan-secret
  namespace: target-namespace
type: Opaque
stringData:
  api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: config-scan-network-policy
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      job-name: config-scan
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: config-scan-portal
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **PVC vs ConfigMap listing**: Using a PVC requires storage provisioning but allows scanning ConfigMap YAML files directly. Listing ConfigMaps via kubectl is simpler but lacks filesystem semantics.
- **InitContainer vs sidecar image**: InitContainer adds startup latency but ensures a minimal base scanner image. A custom image with yq pre-installed reduces complexity but increases maintenance.

## Why This Is Asked
Assess ability to constrain scheduling to hardware and perform safe rolling updates for GPU workloads.

## Key Concepts
- NodeSelector and taints/tolerations
- GPU resource requests/limits
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- RollingUpdate strategy and preStop
- Verification and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ai-processor
  namespace: ml
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ai-processor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ai-processor
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        hardware: gpu
      tolerations:
      - key: hardware
        operator: Equal
        value: gpu
        effect: NoSchedule
      containers:
      - name: ai-processor
        image: your-image:tag
        resources:
          requests:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            memory: "2Gi"
            cpu: "500m"
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            memory: "4Gi"
            cpu: "1000m"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /live
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 1
      maxSurge: 1
```

## Verification Under Load
1. Deploy and verify pods schedule on GPU nodes: `kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide`
2. Check GPU allocation: `kubectl describe nodes | grep nvidia.com/gpu`
3. Load test with concurrent requests while monitoring pod health
4. Verify rolling updates maintain availability: `kubectl rollout status deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
5. Monitor GPU utilization during load: `nvidia-smi` on target nodes

## Rollback Strategy
1. Use deployment revision history: `kubectl rollout history deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
2. Quick rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
3. For critical issues, scale to zero then redeploy previous stable version
4. Monitor rollback progress and verify pod health and GPU allocation
